description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}) as your last tool call and then stop. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your turn is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

1	**Known, disclosed, NOT fixed in this step (Tier 1 / cross-cutting, needs UI-designer sign-off, not this build's authority to resolve):** `text.muted` (`grey[300]`, `#969696`) fails WCAG AA contrast against white at the sizes this build renders it (measured 2.95:1, needs 4.5:1) — confirmed via the real Storybook a11y test-runner, not assumed. This is not new to this step or this epic: `colour.ts`'s own existing comment already flags `grey[300]` as an unresolved Handover self-contradiction (`#969696` vs `#939393` — checked: the alternate value doesn't fix the contrast problem either, both are too light). The same token is already shipped in 10+ other components across the storefront (footer, product card, product price, size chip, button, subscribe modal, icons) — this may already be a live accessibility issue outside this epic entirely, not something this step introduced. Ship to the current spec value per this repo's own established precedent for exactly this situation (`colour.ts`'s own "shipping the current value, confirm with the UI designer" comment) — raise with the UI designer post-build, do not silently drop it and do not invent a replacement value unilaterally.
2	
3	**Also found by this step's own Scorer (2026-09-19), not this step's to fix:** `product-quantity-picker.tsx` (Tier 2, in B3's manifest) now has zero real callers anywhere in the app. `product-item/index.tsx` dropped its import in step 3.5/commit `c426c4ef` when `ZimmQuantityStepper` was wired in to replace it as the real interactive control, and nothing else under `overrides/` ever imported it — confirmed via `grep -rn "from '\./product-quantity-picker'" overrides/`, which returns exactly one hit, the component's own `product-quantity-picker.test.tsx`. This makes the file's previously-cited live-region defect (reads the static `product.quantity` prop, never the live value) moot for the shopper-facing UI rather than fixed — nobody sees it fire at all anymore, correct or not, since nothing renders the component. Per Hard Rule #9 (never delete a file without being explicitly asked), this build leaves it mounted-but-uncalled rather than deleting it — same shape as the base `AddToCartModal`/`/cart` page pattern this epic already carries elsewhere (see HANDOFF.md's "Settled — do not reopen"). Flagged for Marcel to decide: delete outright (Tier 2, needs the same owner sign-off as any other Tier 2 change) or leave as-is.
4	
5	---
6	
7	### B4 — SFCC-250 + 272
8	
9	#### Step 4.1 — The merge call (must come first)
10	
11	**Consequence first.** Today, passwordless OTP sign-in from the wishlist auth drawer does **not** merge baskets. SLAS switches the session to the registered customer and the guest basket is **orphaned — the shopper's items are gone, not miscounted.** Until this is fixed, SFCC-250's AC5 has nothing to cap and SFCC-272's AC8 has no cart item left to move. It is step one of B4 by necessity, not by preference.
12	
13	**Mechanism.** Base `use-auth-modal.js` pairs its own passwordless flow with a `mergeBasket` call. `useWishlistAuthDrawer` reimplemented passwordless login for the drawer and did not carry the merge across. The social-IDP route is fine (it redirects through base `social-login-redirect`, which merges); create-account correctly skips (a new customer has no prior basket). Only `LoginPasswordlessUser` is affected. `grep -rn "mergeBasket" overrides/` is empty — no Zimmermann code merges anything.
14	
15	**Changes.** Add a Zimmermann-owned `mergeBasket` call in `overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`, with `productItemMergeMode: 'sum_quantities'` and `createDestinationBasket: true`.
16	
17	**Corrected 2026-09-19, before this step's Implementer was dispatched — the exact call site above was wrong, found by reading base's real mechanism instead of this paragraph's own original summary of it.** This originally said "at the point `loginPasswordless.mutateAsync` succeeds... around line 230" (i.e., inside `handleOtpVerification`). Base's own `use-auth-modal.js` does **not** call `handleMergeBasket` from its own equivalent of `handleOtpVerification` at all — it calls it from a separate `useEffect(() => {...}, [isRegistered])` that fires once the customer's registered state actually flips true, paired with `onLoginSuccess()`. `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` already has the exact structural equivalent of that effect (its own `isRegistered` effect that calls `onClose()`/`onAuthSuccess?.()`) — the merge call belongs there, alongside `onAuthSuccess?.()`, not inside `handleOtpVerification`. Reasoning: `loginPasswordless.mutateAsync` resolving only means the SDK set the session; `isRegistered` (derived from `useCustomerType()`) is the signal that the rest of the customer-dependent state has actually caught up, which is presumably why base itself waits for it rather than firing merge directly off the raw mutation promise.
18	
19	Also corrected the same day: base additionally gates its own call on `hasBasketItem && prevAuthType === 'guest'` (via `useCustomerBaskets` + `usePrevious(customerType)`) — skip a pointless merge call when the guest basket is empty. This build deliberately does **not** replicate that guard (Marcel's call, 2026-09-19, asked directly): the `prevAuthType === 'guest'` half is already structurally guaranteed here for free — `handleTriggerClick` never opens this drawer at all when the customer is already registered, so every path that can reach the `isRegistered` effect's merge call started from a guest session by construction, with no `usePrevious` needed. The `hasBasketItem` half is deliberately skipped: replicating it would mean wiring a brand-new basket-loading dependency into a hook that has never needed one, on a step already flagged (pass criterion 4 below) as having no CODEOWNERS coverage to catch a subtle timing mistake — and the failure mode of getting that new dependency's timing wrong (merge silently skipped when it shouldn't be) is the exact "shopper's items are gone" bug this whole step exists to close. The failure mode of *not* having the check (one occasional harmless merge-call on an empty basket) is strictly cheaper. Call unconditionally inside the effect; no `useCustomerBaskets`, no `usePrevious`, no `customerType` needed.
20	
21	`sum_quantities`, not the SDK default `higher_quantity`, because AC5's "combined quantity exceeds the maximum" only works if quantities add. **This changes every merge, not just over-max ones** — a guest adds one dress, signs in a week later, the account already had it: today they get one, with summing they get two. Marcel accepted this explicitly. It must go in a comment on SFCC-250 (deferred to post-build) because no AC describes it and a tester finding it otherwise has no way to know two items is intended.
22	
23	**Pass criteria.**
24	1. `useWishlistAuthDrawer.test.tsx` asserts `mergeBasket` is called exactly once on passwordless success, with `productItemMergeMode: 'sum_quantities'` and `createDestinationBasket: true`.
25	2. It asserts `mergeBasket` is **not** called on the create-account route (base deliberately skips register).
26	3. It asserts the social-IDP route is untouched — no second merge added on top of base `social-login-redirect`'s.
27	4. **Regression gate on the other three consumers.** The hook is consumed by `header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu`, `product-view` and (new) the cart. Existing tests for all four still pass, and the PR body names all four as the change's blast radius. This is a shared hook with four call sites and **no CODEOWNERS entry** (see open question 3) — the review that would normally catch a mistake here is not automatically requested.
28	5. The hook's exported signature is **unchanged**. A signature change would need a team RFC (AGENTS.md "When to Stop").
29	6. Live verification is **deferred** per §7 — the code is in scope, the defect ticket and the live proof are not. Say so in the PR body so nobody reads the merge as verified.
30	
31	#### Step 4.2 — `useCartMergeAndCap`
32	
33	**Changes.** One shared function called by both the post-auth callback and the render guard — one implementation, not two copies.
34	
35	Settled shape, all of it: threshold **`>=`** not `==` (a line already holding 4 must fail the check, or the `+` stays live exactly when it matters); scope is **per line item**, not per SKU (the SKU is already size + colour, so in normal shopping one line is one SKU); cap **consolidates to one line at 3** (free — `sum_quantities` already produces a single merged line item); callback order **merge → cap → 272's wishlist resume** (the wishlist move acts on a line the merge may have just consolidated and the cap just reduced; reversing it moves a quantity the shopper never saw); render guard is a secondary backstop that **no-ops while `useIsMutating()` is non-zero**, so it cannot race the callback; **keep the loop guard** — one correction in flight, one attempt per basket version, then stop and surface an error, because a write-on-render without it can rate-limit a shopper out of their own basket; **no action on the brief 4-then-3 flash** — observe real behaviour first.
36	
37	**Pass criteria.**
38	1. Unit tests: line at 2 with max 3 → no change. Line at 3 → no change (`>=` boundary, the case `==` gets wrong is 4). Line at 4 → reduced to 3. Line at 5 → reduced to 3. Two lines of the same SKU at 2 each after a `sum_quantities` merge → one consolidated line at 3.
39	2. `useIsMutating()` non-zero → function returns without issuing a write. Asserted, not assumed.
40	3. Loop guard: two consecutive invocations against the **same** basket version issue exactly **one** write. A server rejection surfaces an error and does **not** retry indefinitely.
41	4. Callback order asserted: with all three armed, merge resolves before cap, and cap resolves before the wishlist resume. Assert on call order, not on final state — final state can look right with the wrong order.
42	5. Max value comes from `maxOrderQuantity.ts` (step 3.4), not a literal.
43	6. **State in the PR body that this is not end-to-end verifiable** until SFCC-268's `afterGET` hook is deployed (gate findings #1/#2 — the TSD is `v0.1 Draft`, Technical Lead sign-off Pending, and the live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product, while Jira has 268 as Ready for SIT). The fallback path is what is being tested.
44	
45	#### Step 4.3 — `useCartMessages`: one handler, one file to swap
46	
47	**Changes.** Every message — success, error, warning — is emitted through **one** function, so SFCC-404 is later a renderer swap in a single file. A marker comment naming SFCC-404 sits at the emit site.
48	
49	Interim surface is the base Chakra toast. **See open question 4 before writing the import line** — `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` does not exist, and creating it is a Tier 2 change this bundle has not budgeted for.
50	
51	Copy (Figma leading, per the cards): single message uses the **product-named** variant, "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist"; already-in-wishlist is "An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist"; max-reached is "An item in your bag has reached maximum quantity". The generic stacked variant ("Item added to Wishlist") is only reachable once 404 lands with real stacking — a toast has no aggregation concept and is always on its own from the shopper's point of view, so the **interim toast uses the product-named copy**. Both divergences from SFCC-272's AC wording go on the deferred Jira comment; the cards are not edited.

### B4 — SFCC-250 + 272

#### Step 4.1 — The merge call (must come first)

**Consequence first.** Today, passwordless OTP sign-in from the wishlist auth drawer does **not** merge baskets. SLAS switches the session to the registered customer and the guest basket is **orphaned — the shopper's items are gone, not miscounted.** Until this is fixed, SFCC-250's AC5 has nothing to cap and SFCC-272's AC8 has no cart item left to move. It is step one of B4 by necessity, not by preference.

**Mechanism.** Base `use-auth-modal.js` pairs its own passwordless flow with a `mergeBasket` call. `useWishlistAuthDrawer` reimplemented passwordless login for the drawer and did not carry the merge across. The social-IDP route is fine (it redirects through base `social-login-redirect`, which merges); create-account correctly skips (a new customer has no prior basket). **Changes.** One shared function called by both the post-auth callback and the render guard — one implementation, not two copies.

import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';

/**
 * Recipe -- SFCC-272 AC2 / SFCC-11 plan step 4.5. Single style, no parts (matches
 * `zimmCartItemActions.css.ts`'s own single-style shape): this recipe owns exactly one thing --
 * the "two columns collapse to one" mechanism (session-notes.md §11.7 / plan.md step 4.5).
 *
 * `ZimmCartDrawer`'s own desktop-breakpoint `body` style (`zimmCartDrawer.css.ts`, the same
 * `@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.xl})` step used here) turns the drawer body into a
 * two-column CSS Grid (`gridTemplateColumns: '22.5rem 26.875rem'`, i.e. 360px/430px) once there
 * is a real cart-item list and totals summary to show side by side. This component *replaces
 * both* of those columns with one piece of content when the bag is empty, so at that same
 * breakpoint its own root must span both grid tracks (`gridColumn: '1 / -1'`) instead of being
 * laid out as an implicit grid item confined to the first (360px) track with 430px of dead space
 * beside it.
 *
 * **No change to `zimmCartDrawer.css.ts` itself** -- which grid tracks a child spans is that
 * child's own property, not its parent's. The drawer's own grid definition is correct and
 * unchanged for every state; this recipe only changes how *this* component behaves as a child of
 * it.
 *
 * `gridColumn` is a no-op everywhere this component is not a grid child -- its own standalone
 * Storybook story, and the mobile/tablet drawer body (`display: flex`, not `grid`) -- so it is
 * safe to declare unconditionally at this breakpoint without checking for a grid parent first.
 *
 * **Verification status (see this step's own report for the full account):** proven directly as
 * a plain object assertion in `zimmCartEmptyState.css.test.ts`, mirroring
 * `zimmCartDrawer.css.test.ts`'s own established pattern for this recipe's sibling. The further,
 * true end-to-end proof -- this component actually rendered full-width with zero dead space
 * *inside the real `ZimmCartDrawer`* -- is not yet possible: `zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx` does not
 * accept this component via `children` at `itemCount === 0` today (it renders its own hardcoded
 * interim placeholder text in that branch instead), so that wiring, and the full visual proof
 * that depends on it, is step 4.6's job, not this one's.
 *
 * Plain object literal, not `defineStyleConfig(...)` -- matching `zimmCartDrawer.css.ts`,
 * `zimmBadge.css.ts` and every other recipe in this codebase that ships its own `.css.test.ts`
 * (`defineStyleConfig`'s return type marks `baseStyle` optional even when the call site always
 * supplies one, which fails `npx tsc --noEmit` on a direct `.baseStyle` property access from a
 * test with no runtime-safe way to narrow it away short of a non-null assertion; every recipe
 * that actually gets read back by a test in this codebase sidesteps that by not using the helper
 * at all -- confirmed directly against `zimmBadge.css.ts`/`zimmSocialButton.css.ts`, both of
 * which have exactly this shape).
 */
export const ZimmCartEmptyState = {
  baseStyle: {
    [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.xl})`]: {
      gridColumn: '1 / -1',
    },
  },
};

1	/**
2	 * NOT in this step's original file manifest -- added deliberately, disclosed here and in this
3	 * step's own report rather than silently. The step's own dispatch text names this exact file and
4	 * calls creating it "acceptable" for proving pass criterion 4 ("Two-to-one column collapse
5	 * asserted in the recipe test") once nesting this component inside the real `ZimmCartDrawer` for
6	 * a live check was confirmed impractical (see `zimmCartEmptyState.css.ts`'s own docblock for why:
7	 * that component does not yet accept this one via `children` at zero items). Mirrors
8	 * `zimmCartDrawer.css.test.ts`'s own established pattern exactly -- a plain object assertion
9	 * against the recipe module, not a rendered DOM check. That is a deliberate choice, not a
10	 * shortcut: Vitest's jsdom environment does not evaluate a real CSS cascade (`@media` conditions
11	 * are not applied the way a real browser applies them, and layout/`getBoundingClientRect` is not
12	 * implemented at all), so a rendered-DOM assertion of *this specific* media-query-gated property
13	 * would not actually prove anything a real browser would agree with. Proving the recipe's own
14	 * declared value is correct and engine-independent; the true live-rendered proof (this component
15	 * actually spanning full width with zero dead space) needs a real browser and is covered by this
16	 * step's own report instead, not by anything under `npm run test`.
17	 */
18	import { describe, test, expect } from 'vitest';
19	import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';
20	import { ZimmCartEmptyState } from './zimmCartEmptyState.css';
21	
22	const DESKTOP_UP = `@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.xl})`;
23	
24	describe('ZimmCartEmptyState recipe', () => {
25	  // SFCC-11 plan step 4.5 pass criterion 4 -- session-notes.md §11.7: "two columns collapse to
26	  // one". Mutation-tested: temporarily changing `gridColumn: '1 / -1'` to `'1 / 2'` in
27	  // zimmCartEmptyState.css.ts (confining the component to the first track, reproducing the real
28	  // bug this recipe exists to prevent) turns this red; restoring it turns it green again.
29	  test("spans both of ZimmCartDrawer's desktop grid columns at the same breakpoint the drawer switches to its two-column grid", () => {
30	    expect(ZimmCartEmptyState.baseStyle[DESKTOP_UP]).toEqual({
31	      gridColumn: '1 / -1',
32	    });
33	  });
34	
35	  // Guards the other half of the same claim: this must NOT be a plain baseStyle property (which
36	  // would apply unconditionally, including on mobile/tablet's single-column flex body, where a
37	  // `grid-column` declaration is harmless but signals a misunderstanding of when it's needed) --
38	  // it must only exist inside the desktop-breakpoint media query, matching exactly where
39	  // `zimmCartDrawer.css.ts`'s own body style switches `display: flex` to `display: grid`.
40	  test('declares no grid-span behaviour outside the desktop breakpoint', () => {
41	    expect((ZimmCartEmptyState.baseStyle as Record<string, unknown>).gridColumn).toBeUndefined();
42	  });
43	});

14	  // useMultiSite().buildUrl unconditionally -- same provider shape zimmCartItemActions/index.stories.tsx

42	 * a non-AU site and a non-identity `buildUrl` (matching the exact `/en-GB${path}` shape
43	 * `recentlyViewed/index.test.tsx` and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.test.ts` already use for the

48	  decorators: [

53	        buildUrl={(path: string) => `/en-GB${path}`}

58	  ],

61	    const cta = canvas.getByRole('link', { name: 'Continue Shopping' });
62	    await expect(cta).toHaveAttribute('href', '/en-GB/');
63	  },

65	
66	// Reproduces ZimmCartDrawer's own desktop-breakpoint `body` grid declaration verbatim
67	// (zimmCartDrawer.css.ts's `baseStyle.body[DESKTOP_UP]`: display grid, 22.5rem/26.875rem tracks,
68	// 140px gap) so this story can prove ZimmCartEmptyState's own gridColumn span against a real
69	// two-column grid parent -- without importing/nesting the real ZimmCartDrawer itself, which does
70	// not yet render this component at zero items at all (see zimmCartEmptyState.css.ts's own
71	// docblock: that wiring is step 4.6's job). This is a *shape-alike* harness for verifying the
72	// span mechanism in isolation, not a claim that it exercises ZimmCartDrawer's actual code.
73	//
74	// `width` is the load-bearing addition over a first draft of this harness (caught live, not
75	// assumed): a plain block `Box` with no explicit width stretches to its own parent's width (here,
76	// the Storybook canvas -- ~1408px at a 1440px viewport), which is NOT what the real
77	// `ZimmCartDrawer` body actually measures. That component's own fixed panel width is 1186px
78	// (plan.md step B1's own math: 128 + 360 + 140 + 430 + 128 = 1186, fixed in commit 3/step 1.1),
79	// so its content box -- after the same 128px `paddingInline` gutter each side
80	// (`var(--zimm-scale-6xl)`, confirmed 128px in `foundation/spacing.ts`) -- is exactly
81	// 1186 - 128 - 128 = 930px: precisely the sum of the two column tracks plus the gap
82	// (360 + 140 + 430 = 930). Left unconstrained, the first draft of this story's own `play`
83	// function failed by comparing this component's width against the harness's own (wrongly wide)
84	// 1408px instead of the real 930px the drawer would actually offer it -- a bug in the harness,
85	// not in the recipe (`getComputedStyle` already showed `gridColumn: '1 / -1'` resolving
86	// correctly even before this fix). Constraining the harness to the real content-box width is
87	// what makes this story an honest stand-in for the real drawer body.
88	const GRID_HARNESS_STYLE = {
89	  display: 'grid',
90	  gridTemplateColumns: '22.5rem 26.875rem',
91	  columnGap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3500)',
92	  width: '58.125rem', // 930px = 22.5rem + 26.875rem + 8.75rem(140px gap) -- see comment above
93	} as const;

95	/**
96	 * Live proof for pass criterion 4 ("Two-to-one column collapse asserted") alongside
97	 * `zimmCartEmptyState.css.test.ts`'s own object-level assertion -- that file proves the recipe
98	 * *declares* `gridColumn: '1 / -1'` at the desktop breakpoint; this story proves it actually
99	 * *takes effect* against a real two-column CSS Grid parent, live-rendered in a real browser
100	 * engine (Vitest's jsdom cannot evaluate this: no real `@media` cascade, and
101	 * `getBoundingClientRect` always returns zeros there -- see that test file's own docblock).
102	 *
103	 * Requires an actual wide (>= the 1280px desktop breakpoint) viewport to mean anything -- this
104	 * repo has no `.storybook` viewport-addon preset configured and no `test-storybook` script (both
105	 * checked before writing this), so this story was verified with an explicit wide viewport driven
106	 * directly against a live Storybook dev server for this step's own report, rather than relying on
107	 * a CI-wired check. The `play` function below still runs (and still means something) any time
108	 * this story is opened in a browser window at or above that width, including the default desktop
109	 * width Storybook's own UI opens at on a normal developer machine.
110	 */
111	export const SpansBothDrawerColumnsAtDesktop: Story = {
112	  decorators: [
113	    (Story) => (
114	      <Box sx={GRID_HARNESS_STYLE} data-testid="grid-harness">
115	        <Story />
116	      </Box>
117	    ),
118	  ],
119	  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
120	    if (window.innerWidth < 1280) {
121	      // Documented, not silently skipped -- see this story's own docblock for why this repo has
122	      // no way to force a wide viewport for every context this play could run in. Deliberate,
123	      // narrow diagnostic (Storybook developer tooling, not app code) -- conventions.md's
124	      // no-console rule targets console.log/console.error, not console.warn.
125	      console.warn('SpansBothDrawerColumnsAtDesktop: viewport is below 1280px, skipping the span assertion.');
126	      return;
127	    }
128	    const canvas = within(canvasElement);
129	    const harness = canvas.getByTestId('grid-harness');
130	    const root = canvas.getByTestId('zimm-cart-empty-state');
131	    const harnessWidth = harness.getBoundingClientRect().width;
132	    const rootWidth = root.getBoundingClientRect().width;
133	    const itemsColumnWidthPx = 22.5 * 16; // 22.5rem items-only track, at a 16px root font size
134	
135	    // Full-width (spans both tracks), not confined to the 360px items column alone.
136	    await expect(rootWidth).toBeGreaterThan(itemsColumnWidthPx);
137	    await expect(Math.round(rootWidth)).toBe(Math.round(harnessWidth));
138	  },
139	};
